name: Luo Weidong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Aurora Mobile Ltd (Nasdaq: JG), Shenzhen
profile: Luo Weidong (Chris Luo) co-founded Shenzhen-based Aurora Mobile (JPush / Jiguang) in 2011 and has been chairman and CEO since May 2012. The mobile developer-services and big-data company, backed by IDG, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs, listed on Nasdaq in 2018; his stake (~30%) is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: PolyU says Aurora Mobile was the first company of its kind to list on Nasdaq (2018); Luo holds an MPhil in computing from PolyU and won its Outstanding Alumni Award for entrepreneurial achievement in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: During COVID-19, Luo led a research team behind a data platform that PolyU credits with supporting epidemic-containment work in 334 Chinese cities. Before Aurora he was GM of Shenzhen Zhiwo Information Technology (2007-2010).

public_contacts.value: Christensen Advisory - Xiaoyan Su, Xiaoyan.Su@christensencomms.com (IR agency named in Aurora Mobile press releases)

notes: Goes by Chris Luo. Some IR pages list ir@aurora-mobile.com instead of ir@jiguang.cn (company rebranding of IR domain). Named 2025 Greater Bay Area Strategic Emerging Industry Youth Leader (Feb 2026 release).

name: Xu Jie
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Phoenix Healthcare Group (now China Resources Medical, HKEX: 1515); current role not publicly reported
profile: Xu Jie (徐捷) founded Phoenix Healthcare, which grew from private hospitals into China's largest private hospital group by beds and visits and listed in Hong Kong in 2013 as the 'first private-hospital stock'. In 2016 China Resources took control; her family vehicle SpeedKey exited and she stepped down as chair. No public role since.
interesting_fact: Phoenix Healthcare's 2013 Hong Kong IPO made it the first listed private-hospital operator from mainland China; it pioneered investing in and managing public and SOE-owned hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2013 IPO prospectus, she bought the Jilin City Trauma Hospital (吉林市创伤医院) in 1988 and personally served as its legal representative and hospital director until 1995, before investing in hospitals in Dalian and Wuxi and founding Beijing Phoenix in 2007 with RMB45m of her own capital.
notes: Very low public profile since the 2016 China Resources takeover; company contacts (China Resources Medical) no longer represent her. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Raman Gupta
current_role: Promoter/long-time director of Metenere group (Metenere Limited, Metenere (Global) Ltd), Delhi; MD role at Metenere Limited reportedly ceased Oct 2024
profile: Raman Gupta is the Delhi-based promoter of Metenere, a non-ferrous metals group producing lead, lead alloys and oxides, aluminium products and tin. He has been a director of Metenere Limited since its 1997 incorporation; registry aggregators indicate a board change/amalgamation in Oct 2024. Hurun India listed him in 2017-2018.
interesting_fact: Metenere describes itself as one of India's biggest lead producers and the only producer of pure tin in India.
notes: Very little public coverage; sources are company-registry aggregators (Tofler, Qorpiq). Company website metenere.com appears to be parked/for sale. No published contact found; any outreach would need a verified company channel.

name: Shen Haiyin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zhiche Youxing Technology (智车优行, brand Singulato / 奇点汽车), Shanghai/Beijing; current status unclear
profile: Shen Haiyin (沈海寅) is an internet executive turned EV entrepreneur: a former VP at Kingsoft and Qihoo 360 and angel investor, he founded Zhiche Youxing in Oct 2014 to build smart EVs under the Singulato (奇点) brand, which raised at least seven rounds through 2020 and made him a Hurun unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: He decided to build cars after driving a Tesla in 2014: 'After experiencing a Tesla, I felt the auto industry was bound to change' (体验过特斯拉的车后，我就感觉汽车行业一定会变天).
deep_cut_fact: Not a total auto outsider: his first job after university was at Shanghai Delphi Automotive Air Conditioning, making car A/C components; in 2000 he moved to Japan and founded three companies there before ~15 years in China's internet industry.
notes: Singulato faced funding/wage-arrears problems and was reported heading toward bankruptcy around 2023 - avoid as a hook. No recent (2024-26) public activity found; no published contact.
